Section 1: Defense Speaking Strategy & Delivery Guidelines

To deliver an outstanding, authoritative thesis defense presentation for Chapter 5, adhere strictly to these executive presentation principles:

Tone & Demeanor Engineered Trust & Authority: Speak clearly and at a measured pace. Avoid casual phrases like "we just put a button here". Instead, use architectural language: "We implemented a server-side permission guard", "This triggers a cryptographic verification email", "State transition enforced by Prisma ORM."
Core Defense Anchor Zero Fake ATS / High-Trust Network: Reiterate frequently that UniCareer is not a generic public job board or an employer applicant tracker. It is a private, university-connected referral network designed to link scholars with alumni mentors.
Three Mandatory Presentation Anchor Rules
  • Point Directly at the Screen: When mentioning badges (e.g. STUDENT · Verified), routes (e.g. /opportunities/post), or modal buttons, physically gesture to the slide screenshot.
  • Connect UI to the Database: Always mention the underlying table powering the view (e.g. "This modal writes directly to our referral_requests relational table").
  • Highlight Security Pre-conditions: Emphasize what unauthorized or unverified users CANNOT do on each screen (e.g. unverified visitors cannot browse full descriptions or send pitches).

Welcome to Chapter 5 — The App in Action

📢 Spoken Script (Word-for-Word)
"Honorable committee members, welcome to Chapter 5: The App in Action.

Up to this point in our defense, we have established the theoretical foundations of UniCareer Community: our functional requirements, UML state machines, and our 30-table relational schema. Now, we demonstrate how those architectural models come to life in a responsive, accessible, pixel-perfect user interface.

Rather than displaying static graphic mockups, Chapter 5 follows complete, real-world user flows: from an unverified student creating an account, to alumni sharing job leads, to direct referral requests and platform governance. Every screen you see here is backed by live database state and server-side authorization guards."
Slide 2 / 8 · User Onboarding Joining Flow /register → Gmail → /community (Admin)

Create Your Account — The Two-Stage Verification Gate

Step 1: Sign-Up Form/register
Step 2: Verification EmailGmail Inbox
Step 3: Admin Review Queue/community
You DoFill the registration form, then click the cryptographic email link.
You GetA confirmed email and an applicant dossier dispatched to the Administrator Verification Queue.
📢 Spoken Script (Word-for-Word)
"Let us begin with our first major user journey: Account Registration and our Two-Stage Verification Gate.

On the left screenshot, on our /register screen titled 'Let’s Start Learning', the applicant selects their active persona: Current Student or Alumnus / Alumna. They provide their legal name, institutional university email address, university student ID number, academic department, and a strong password.

Here is our first critical architectural rule: submitting this form does not log the user in. The system locks their student ID and department into the database and immediately routes them to /verify-email.

In the center screenshot, you see the actual transactional email dispatched through our SMTP mailer with the subject 'Verify your UniCareer Community account'. When the applicant clicks 'Confirm Email', Better Auth verifies the cryptographic token. But notice: autoSignInAfterVerification is strictly set to false. The user is still blocked from logging in.

Instead, the email verification hook promotes the user's emailVerified flag to true and dispatches their dossier to the Administrator Verification Queue, as shown in the right screenshot. In the Admin’s view at /community, the applicant appears with an amber PENDING badge alongside one-click administrative actions: Verify, Suspend, or Inspect Profile.

This ensures zero unverified outsiders can ever infiltrate the campus network."
Architectural Micro-Details to Point Out
  • Password Encryption: Passwords are hashed with scrypt through Better Auth and stored in the isolated accounts table to prevent accidental JSON leaks.
  • Tamper-Resistant Identity: Student ID and department are locked at registration; students cannot edit their identity to spoof another academic department.
  • HTTP Guard: Unapproved logins receive an explicit HTTP 403 Forbidden with error code EMAIL_NOT_VERIFIED or redirect parameter ?error=pending_admin_approval.

Log In to Your Dashboard — Gateway to the Community

Step 1: Sign-In Gateway/login
Step 2: Home Feed/feed
You DoSign in with your verified credentials after receiving the official administrative approval email.

📢 Spoken Script (Word-for-Word)
"Once an administrator officially validates the applicant's credentials, an automated approval email is dispatched, and the user can proceed to the /login screen on the left.

If an unapproved user attempts to sign in prior to administrative clearance, the login interface traps the attempt, displays an amber 'Awaiting Administrator Approval' warning banner, and prevents session creation.

Upon authenticated sign-in with verified credentials, the server establishes a secure cryptographic session token in the sessions table and routes the user directly to the home dashboard at /feed, visible on the right.

The navigation bar transitions from the public marketing state into the authenticated platform header: displaying the user's initials avatar, institutional verification badge, notifications counter, and quick-action launcher buttons to Browse Opportunities, Member Network, and Post Opportunity."

On the left is our post composer. A member can provide an optional headline, select their specific post taxonomy — Discussion & Questions, Referral Request, or Achievement — and compose their message. Share a Job — Verified Career Opportunities

Step 1: Opportunity Post Form/opportunities/post
Step 2: Author Management Console/opportunities/my
You DoSubmit role details, academic criteria, application deadline, and official company portal URL.
You GetA live community opportunity lead that you can manage, close, or remove.
📢 Spoken Script (Word-for-Word)
"In UniCareer Community, job postings are not scraped from random search engines. They are shared directly by verified alumni mentors and authorized members.

On the left is the Share a Career Opportunity form at /opportunities/post. It features a two-tab interface: 'Edit Opening' and 'Live Card Preview'.

The form captures four distinct data groups:
1. Target Company name and verified company affiliation.
2. Role Title, Employment Type (INTERNSHIP, FULL_TIME, CONTRACT), Workplace Setting (REMOTE, HYBRID, ON_SITE), and Location.
3. Academic criteria: Minimum CGPA thresholds, target departments, and required tech skills.
4. The application gateway: The mandatory official external destination URL (such as the company's official career portal) and an optional alumni inquiry email.

Once submitted, the post transitions immediately to the author's management dashboard on the right at /opportunities/my.

Here, the author can monitor how many students have saved or viewed their listing, inspect full details, or click Close Opportunity when the hiring quota is met. The server enforces strict ownership: only the original poster or a platform admin can close or remove a listing."

On the left, on /opportunities, students can filter verified opportunities by Role Type, Workplace Setting, Department, and Minimum CGPA. Each card highlights key metadata at a glance: salary or stipend, location, required tech stack badges, and application cutoff dates.

When a student clicks 'View Details', they arrive at the opportunity gateway in the center screenshot. Notice the Opportunity Gate box:
First, it displays the verified cutoff date.
Second, it features our prominent 'Mail Me / Contact for Referral' inquiry button if the poster supplied a contact email.
And third, when clicking 'Apply on Company Site', our modal appears: it provides the outbound link to the official company hiring portal (such as bKash or Brain Station 23 Careers), while offering a checkbox to 'Save this in My Applications' with private candidate interview notes.

Now, observe the third screen on the right: /calendar. The moment the student tracks that application, the database automatically synchronizes the job's deadline onto their calendar — circled here on December 24th.

The calendar color-codes events across Applications, Interviews, Saved Deadlines, and Reminders. Our automated background reminder engine alerts the student 72 hours before any tracked opportunity expires."
Slide 7 / 8 · High-Trust Networking Referral Flow /feed → /profile/[id] (Modal)

Ask an Alumnus for a Referral — Dual-Mode 'Mail Me' System

Channel 1: Feed Referral Request/feed
Channel 2: Direct Mail Me Modal/profile/[id]
You DoSubmit a referral pitch publicly in the feed or privately via the alumnus's profile modal.
You GetA 1-click formatted email template, direct contact capability, and an in-app tracked audit record.
📢 Spoken Script (Word-for-Word)
"This brings us to one of our most praised features: The High-Trust Alumni Referral System.

Students can request referrals in two distinct ways:

First, via the public feed on the left: a student publishes a post tagged as 'Referral Request' detailing their interest in backend engineering at Chaldal. A verified alumnus working at Chaldal replies directly in the comments offering mentorship.

Second, via direct profile contact on the right: when viewing an alumnus's profile, clicking 'Contact for Referral' opens our specialized dual-mode modal.

Notice the two tabs:
1. Mode 1 — Direct Email ('Mail Me'): Designed for busy alumni who prefer handling correspondence in Gmail or Outlook. The student inputs their target role and qualifications pitch. The system automatically constructs a professional email with pre-filled subject and body. The student can click 'Open in Email App' to launch their mail client via mailto:, or click 'Copy Template' for webmail.
2. Status Tracking: By keeping the checkbox ticked, the request is simultaneously logged in the database so the student can track when they reached out.
3. Mode 2 — In-App Dossier: If the alumnus prefers privacy, the modal submits an internal referral request stored in our referral_requests table, notifying the alumnus on their /referrals dashboard.

This strikes the perfect balance between alumni privacy, convenience, and student accountability."
Slide 8 / 8 · Platform Safety & Governance Admin Flow /admin · Overview & Content Reports

Admin: Keep It Safe — Operational Command & Moderation

Console 1: Operations Overview/admin · Overview
Console 2: Content Reports/admin · Content Reports
You DoMonitor platform metrics, verify member dossiers, and inspect flagged community content.
You GetA compliant, spam-free university network where every administrative action is logged in audit trails.
📢 Spoken Script (Word-for-Word)
"Finally, we present Platform Governance & Administrative Moderation.

On the left is the Admin Command Center at /admin. At a glance, administrators receive critical operational telemetry:
- A notification alert for pending verification dossiers requiring human review.
- A live count of total verified members, active listings, submitted applications, and feed posts.
- Navigation tabs covering Verification Requests, Member Directory, Content Reports, Corporate Profiles, and Platform Analytics.

On the right is the Content Reports Moderation Console.
When community members report a post or comment for harassment, spam, or false recruitment details, the item enters this queue.

Administrators have three distinct enforcement actions:
1. Dismiss: If the report is invalid, marking it resolved.
2. Remove: Soft-deletes or hides the offending post from public feeds.
3. Suspend Member: Immediately revokes the offender's access across the platform.

Every administrative action triggers an immutable entry in our audit_logs table, recording the administrator's ID, the affected entity, the timestamp, and the exact justification. Furthermore, server-side permissions enforce that administrators cannot suspend their own accounts.

This ensures UniCareer Community remains a safe, prestigious, and compliant institutional asset for the university."

Section 3: Anticipated Committee Defense Q&A Sheet

Prepare for these specific technical inquiries frequently asked by academic software engineering defense panels:

Committee Question Recommended Technical Answer
1. "Why do you use external application links instead of building a resume upload & review ATS?" Institutional Reality & Privacy: Employers hire exclusively through their official corporate applicant portals (such as bKash, Brain Station 23, or Vercel). Building a fake internal ATS would force students to upload sensitive CVs into an unmonitored portal that employers never check. By redirecting to official hiring URLs while offering private application tracking with calendar deadlines, we protect candidate data privacy while maintaining complete personal accountability.
2. "What prevents an unauthorized student from accessing alumni contact emails?" Multi-Layer Privacy Shield: On the database level, Profile.showEmail defaults to false. In our service layer (lib/services/profile.ts), the user's email address is stripped from the returned JSON payload unless the viewer is the account owner, a platform administrator, or the user explicitly set showEmail: true. Furthermore, our referral modal falls back gracefully to the In-App Dossier queue when an email is private.
3. "How does the system prevent student spam in referral requests?" Database & Validation Constraints: We enforce: 1. A strict 20-character minimum and 2,000-character maximum for pitch messages. 2. Rate limiting on the API route (POST /api/referrals). 3. One active pending referral request per student per opportunity. 4. Complete blocking of self-referrals (requesterId cannot equal recipientId).
4. "How is data consistency maintained when an opportunity is deleted or closed?" Relational Integrity & Cascade Rules: In prisma/schema.prisma, bookmarks, applications, and comments use onDelete: Cascade, ensuring clean garbage collection without orphaned rows. Furthermore, in referral requests and posts, the foreign key uses onDelete: SetNull, ensuring that private conversation dossiers between students and alumni remain preserved even if the linked job posting is closed or removed.
